RagShortTexts: Spanning and loading a crossbow require time and working space.
Damaged strings impair tension and safe use.

Variants.Content: A crossbow separates spanning from aiming, but the user must span, load and inspect its particular mechanism. Strings and bolts require careful storage. Reloading leaves little freedom to hold a shield, so position and protection by companions affect its usefulness.
After shooting, a crossbowman needs room to span and a clear line past companions. Frayed strings or ill-fitting bolts make hurried loading hazardous; cover is valuable during the pause.
Crossbow service costs strings, shafts and practice, with loading room on the walls. Recruiting users does not make every stored bow compatible with every bundle of bolts.
Bolt and string makers need suitable materials, and buyers inspect rather than merely count bundles. Damp storage increases upkeep; neglected items may disable weapons when the town needs them.
